adoption.notes: From a0dd23c it implements gateway.state_directory: the load rules, with the state-directory corpus run through its configuration loader, and the start and mark requirements as they stood at 404cbcb, the marker, the lock and the mark of its message signing clock. It has no release, and its evidence is host tests and CI, not deployed provisioning, Linux, power loss or HIL. At ec162f4 a reading against this section at f37845f found each of the seven divergences recorded at a0dd23c addressed: one write of the mark outstanding at a time, off the lock that issues values and never below a mark written before; a 1,000 ms write bound that opens an episode, with a value waiting at most that bound and never past an episode's opening; paced retries while an episode is open; an episode closing only on a write covering the last value issued; degraded in the heartbeat and site health; a start refused when its first write fails or passes the bound; and a stop that ends the process with status 1 without releasing the lock once a release quiescence bound of 5 s passes. A review then reproduced a divergence the seven did not name: after the stop decision the gateway still admits work, because its broker callback gate closes only during later cleanup, contrary to rule 13. The current snapshot is unassessed, and the assessment below is of a0dd23c and stays as recorded. Its evidence is host tests and CI, including child-process tests of the exit and of a competing owner, not a real hung disk, uninterruptible I/O, power loss, Linux deployment or HIL.

assessment.method: The gateway's signing clock, state directory and shutdown path were read at a0dd23c against this version's gateway.state_directory section at c2bed1a, by the specs and gateway sessions and an independent review.
divergences: A value past the reservation is persisted under the clock's lock with no bound, or waits with no bound for a background extension in flight, so a write that never returns blocks every signer instead of opening an episode under rule 11.
The start's first write has no bound: a start whose first write never returns never ends, contrary to rule 7.

No mark attempted earlier is kept: only marks at or below the last successful write are skipped, so after a failed write that may have landed and a wall-clock step back, a lower mark can be written, contrary to rule 9.
A failing write is retried with every value past the reservation, once per message, not paced under rule 11.
There is no episode state: nothing reports degraded in the heartbeat or site health, only a warning each time writes start failing, contrary to rule 11.
The clock is closed after broker callbacks and posture fetches are joined, not at the decision to stop, so work in flight can still sign and start writes during a stop, contrary to rule 13.
Shutdown waits for an outstanding write with no bound, contrary to rule 13's quiescence bound and non-zero exit.

notes: Created by the baseline audit of gateway-config/v1 as the destination of its one semantic post-freeze hunk: `gateway.device_ids` became a required key at 4265583, which the gateway has enforced since 3081e4c, refusing a configuration valid under v1's freeze revision. The text is v1's as it stood on main before the audit removed that requirement from v1. The opt-in evidence-carriage extension and its ten vectors land here, under A4's compatibility conditions. It is amended in place to add `gateway.state_directory`, the gateway's own durable state, which holds the mark of the gateway's message signing clock under gateway-api/v2 Senders, with its load rules and their corpus. Amended in place for a mark write that stalls: a write of the mark that stalls opens an episode after a 1,000 ms write bound, during which signing goes on uncovered with one write outstanding and paced retries; a mark never overwrites a higher completed one; the lock ends only once no write is outstanding or with the process; and the state directory must be on local storage, which the gateway does not check.
